definitions.explanation: The number five. A central number in Japanese culture, found in many traditional concepts. Straightforward to use with most counters.

examples.english: I wake up at five o'clock.

examples.japanese: {五|ご}{人|にん}{家族|かぞく}です。
{五|ご}{月|がつ}は{気持|きも}ちいい{季節|きせつ}です。
{友達|ともだち}と{約束|やくそく}があるから、{五|ご}{時|じ}までに{家|いえ}に{帰|かえ}らなければなりません。
examples.english: I have plans with a friend, so I have to be home by five o'clock.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{会社|かいしゃ}では{週|しゅう}に{五|ご}{日|にち}{働|はたら}くのが{普通|ふつう}で、{土曜日|どようび}と{日曜日|にちようび}は{休|やす}みになっています。
examples.english: In Japanese companies, it's normal to work five days a week, with Saturday and Sunday off.

notes:
{五|ご} is the Sino-Japanese reading for five, used with most counters and in compounds.

READINGS:
- ご: Sino-Japanese (used with counters like {個|こ}, {人|にん}, {時|じ})
- いつ: appears in いつつ (native counter for objects)

COMMON USES:
- {五|ご}{時|じ}: 5 o'clock
- {五|ご}{月|がつ}: May
- {五|ご}{日|にち}: the 5th (of the month)
- {五|ご}{人|にん}: five people
- {五|いつ}つ: five (objects)

CULTURAL:
- {五|ご}{感|かん}: the five senses
- {五|ご}{輪|りん}: the Olympic rings; also Buddhist five elements
- {五|ご}{十|じゅっ}{音|おん}: the Japanese syllabary order

NOTE:
Five is considered a balanced number in East Asian cultures, associated with the five elements.
